comparisons.evidence: Q spans materially different mechanisms: a "portable business entity," "objective risk triggers," standardised "Care-Hours Futures," and an asset-conversion "Home-Equity-to-Habitat Swap." P is broad, but more of its pool clusters around planners, concierges, memberships and coordination services such as "Continuity OS," "Care Circle," "Destination Planner" and "Trusted Local Proxy Network."

Q reaches further with mechanisms such as "Reverse Timeshare Market Maker," "Care-Hours Futures" and "Home-Equity-to-Habitat Swap." P has strong departures—especially "Friendship Portability Protocol" and "Nomad Failure Rehearsal"—but more of its remaining set resembles sophisticated extensions of familiar travel and retirement services.

Q explicitly derives finalists from named rules in "migratory-bird ecology" and "financial derivatives," including "Options preserve future choice" and "Illiquid or uncertain resources become usable through pooling, exchange and standardisation." The resulting "Care-Hours Futures" and "Home-Equity-to-Habitat Swap" depend on those structures. P contains metaphors such as "friendship as portable infrastructure" but no named cross-domain rule generating a finalist.

Both identify threshold-avoidance software as the strongest entry point. P calls the "Retirement Residency Simulator" the "Best entry product" because it avoids requiring a global physical network; Q launches "Jurisdiction Autopilot" because it has a "narrow user, observable pain, low operational burden and a fast software MVP." Both are credible strongest choices for the brief.

Q names testable assumptions and concrete failure modes, such as "Countries and clients will accept a standardised intermediary structure," "False triggers, unused reserved capacity," and "Provider insolvency, labour shortages and uneven quality." P mostly supplies aggregate labels such as "Operational difficulty: High" and broad moat claims like "trusted partners, and high switching costs," with less direct confrontation of failure.

Q repeatedly states precise causal insights: "Family anxiety is often a governance failure, not a sensor or communication failure" and "Owning money does not guarantee that a trusted person will appear." P also has sharp formulations—"friendship as portable infrastructure" and "reassurance without infantilization"—but Q connects such insights more consistently to product mechanisms and buyer behaviour.

note: The biggest difference is that Q converts explicit cross-domain rules into structurally novel products and then stress-tests them, while P offers a rich but more service-centric portfolio.
